lead: The National Assembly suspended all legislative engagement with South Africa over renewed xenophobic attacks, as a Nigerian bishop was reported killed in Johannesburg. Suspected herdsmen killed four mobile policemen and eight villagers in Benue, ASUU threatened to resume its strike, and the Ondo death toll from a suspected poisoned drink rose to 30. Brent crude passed $107 and the Dangote refinery raised its petrol price to N1,350 a litre.

items.h: National Assembly suspends engagement with South Africa over xenophobia
items.s: The National Assembly halted all official legislative contact with South Africa, including visits, conferences and parliamentary exchanges, over renewed xenophobic attacks on Nigerians and other Africans.

items.h: Nigerian bishop reported killed in Johannesburg
items.s: The Nigerian Citizens Association South Africa said Bishop Taiwo Michael Fakunle, 58, was killed in Johannesburg.

items.h: Four mobile policemen and eight villagers killed in Benue attack
items.s: Suspected armed herdsmen attacked Ayilamo in Logo Local Government Area, killing four mobile police officers and eight residents.

items.h: ASUU threatens to resume strike without further notice
items.s: The Academic Staff Union of Universities warned that it may restart its suspended national strike unless federal and state governments address unpaid salaries and the 2025 agreement.

items.h: Ondo poisoned drink death toll rises to 30
items.s: Thirty people have now died after drinking a suspected poisoned local alcohol in Odigbo, and about 50 others are in hospital.

items.h: Dangote raises petrol to N1,350 as Brent tops $107
items.s: The Dangote refinery increased its petrol gantry price by N85 to N1,350 a litre as Brent crude passed $107 a barrel for the first time since May.

items.h: EFCC and FBI probe alleged diversion of US-funded health programme money
items.s: The EFCC said it will trace funds under US-supported HIV and tuberculosis programmes in Nigeria following allegations of mismanagement.

items.h: Shettima represents Tinubu at BRICS summit in India
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima arrived in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit as Nigeria seeks closer ties with the bloc.

items.h: Mob kills man who stabbed Sokoto cleric after Friday prayers
items.s: Cleric Malam Musa Lukuwa was stabbed after Juma'at prayers in Sokoto, and his alleged attacker was beaten to death by a crowd.

items.h: Bandits raid Sokoto village as police open investigation
items.s: Bandits attacked Girekau in Kebbe Local Government Area, with reports of killings and abductions, and police began an investigation.

items.h: INEC rejects Obi's plan for parallel results collation
items.s: INEC said only it can collate and announce election results, after Peter Obi proposed a parallel tally that the ADC endorsed.

items.h: Atiku says his subsidy plan shifts support to production
items.s: Atiku Abubakar said the Presidency distorted the Dangote refinery's concerns to discredit his proposal, which he said would subsidise production rather than imports.

items.h: Audit says aviation ministry paid N522m for undelivered guns
items.s: According to the Auditor-General's 2024 report, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development spent N522.49 million on weapons and ammunition that never arrived.

items.h: FG begins N18bn payment to former Nigeria Airways workers
items.s: The government started paying N18 billion in severance benefits owed to 2,700 former staff of the defunct national airline.

items.h: Immigration extends UK passport exercise to 3 October
items.s: The Nigeria Immigration Service extended its special passport intervention in the United Kingdom after complaints of delays.

items.h: Kaduna to implement ASUU pay deal at KASU from October
items.s: Governor Uba Sani approved the 2025 FGN-ASUU salary agreement for Kaduna State University staff and urged lecturers to end their strike.

items.h: Police and ADC dispute tear-gassing of Kaduna rally
items.s: ADC governorship candidate Mohammed Ashiru accused security operatives of attacking party members at a rally, which police disputed.

items.h: Dangote refinery buys 16m barrels of Nigerian crude for October
items.s: Reuters reported, citing four sources, that the refinery bought at least 16 million barrels of local crude for October delivery.

items.h: US delivers military equipment to Nigerian Air Force
items.s: US Africa Command said it delivered equipment to the Nigerian Air Force to support counter-terrorism operations.

items.h: Fire damages Idu train station in Abuja
items.s: An electrical fault caused a fire at the Abuja-Kaduna line's Idu station; the Nigerian Railway Corporation said operations have resumed.

items.h: Bosun Tijani withdraws from ITU deputy secretary-general race
items.s: Communications Minister Bosun Tijani pulled out of the contest for the International Telecommunication Union post despite his nomination by the President.

items.h: Air Peace chief says Tinubu will rescue aviation sector
items.s: Allen Onyema said the President's intervention will address IATA's ranking of Nigeria as the hardest place to run an airline.

items.h: NNPC opens smart fuel station in Abuja, plans 70 more
items.s: NNPC Retail commissioned a smart filling station in the FCT, aims to open 70 more in six months, and said no jobs will be lost.

items.h: CBN targets zero failed transactions by 2028
items.s: The Central Bank wants a faster, more reliable payment system by 2028 but faces infrastructure problems, BusinessDay reported.

items.h: D'Tigress players receive $100,000 each for AfroBasket title
items.s: Each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000 under the presidential reward for winning the 2025 Women's AfroBasket.

items.h: Amusan wins 100m hurdles silver in Budapest
items.s: Tobi Amusan took silver at the first World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest on Friday.

items.h: Reps spokesman clears Wike over loans
items.s: House deputy spokesman Philip Agbese said FCT Minister Nyesom Wike did not take loans without National Assembly approval.

items.h: FCT APC launches drive to end opposition's hold on Abuja
items.s: The APC in the FCT began grassroots mobilisation to win the capital in the 2027 presidential poll.

items.h: Former APC chieftain joins ADC in Gombe
items.s: ADC governorship candidate Bala Tinka received Adamu Abdullahi Masad, a former APC leader, into the party.

items.h: Buni sets up APC reconciliation committees in Yobe
items.s: Governor Mai Mala Buni inaugurated committees for the three senatorial districts to settle internal disputes.

items.h: Uba Sani appoints three commissioners and 45 aides
items.s: The Kaduna governor named three new commissioners, 45 aides and 40 board members.

items.h: Anambra monarchs give Remi Tinubu chieftaincy title
items.s: Traditional rulers from 179 communities conferred the title Ugo Eze Anambra on the First Lady.

items.h: Group petitions House over Ajaokuta iron ore lease
items.s: A civil society group, Public Accountability and Transparency International, asked the House of Representatives to examine the sub-lease that hands National Iron Ore Mining Company operations to Premium Steel.

items.h: Ogun and FG pay retirees' benefits
items.s: Ogun released N6.75 billion to clear gratuities and pension arrears, while the federal government settled about N1.1 billion owed to 175 retired civil servants.

items.h: Katsina launches $1m flood and drought project for farmers
items.s: The 12-month project, run with Mercy Corps Nigeria, will protect vulnerable farming communities.

items.h: Nigeria and Burkina Faso seek closer trade ties
items.s: The two countries are working to expand trade, investment, transport and digital cooperation, Nigeria's ambassador said.

items.h: Kebbi registers 3,257 for 2027 Hajj as Saudi plans reforms
items.s: Kebbi's pilgrims agency remitted N21.5 billion in fares, and a minister backed Saudi Arabia's plan to shift 30 per cent of Nigeria's pilgrims to a new arrangement.

items.h: Julius Berger and Lagos discuss infrastructure for $1trn economy
items.s: Julius Berger and the Lagos government set out a shared vision on infrastructure and public-private investment at the firm's annual soirée.

items.h: UBA Foundation opens N41m essay competition
items.s: The bank's foundation launched its 2026 national essay contest for secondary school students.
